sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between poverty and wealth in spiritual service, where wealth represents a level beyond intellectual limitation.

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing,
that the matter of wealth in its simple sense is,
as brought above
(section 3)
from the maamar,
that the wealthy person has not only his needs but is influenced with an abundance of influence.
And based on this,
the difference between a poor person, even when he has enough for his lack, and a wealthy person is in two matters.
That even in those things that exist also for the poor person,
it is not comparable to the wealthy person.
For the poor person, from his own perspective, is lacking even these things
(as above there),
and only in actuality do these things exist for him.
And that the wealthy person is influenced with an abundance of influence — an abundance of influence that does not exist at all for the poor person.
And ostensibly it must be said,
that in spirituality,
these two matters are dependent on each other.
That in order that the matters that he is compelled in
(his sufficient lack)
should be for him not in a manner of receiving them from others but from his own self,
it is specifically through the abundance of influence that is above filling the lack.
And the matter in avodah is,
that when a person's avodah is only according to the comprehension of his intellect,
then,
in addition to the avodah being in measure and limitation
(his sufficient lack),
he is lacking
(in inwardness)
even this avodah,
because from the perspective of comprehension there is a place for the opposite.
And in order that his avodah before Hashem should be in a manner that no place for the opposite remains in him, it is specifically through avodah that is above measure and limitation — wealth.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the three levels in the spiritual worlds: Memaleh Kol Almin, Sovev Kol Almin, and Atzmus Ein Sof, corresponding to filling lack, supplying extra needs, and wealth.

translations.translation: And in order to explain the matter of wealth that is above filling the lack,
the maamar46 prefaces,
that even in filling the lack there are two matters,
as it is written "enough for his lack that he lacks" and our sages of blessed memory said "that he lacks — even a horse to ride upon and a servant to run before him."
That is, "enough for his lack" is that one must provide for him all the things needed for each person,
and afterwards it adds "that he lacks,"
that one must provide for him also that which he lacks.
(A horse to ride upon and a servant to run before him)
from the aspect that this is his way47.
And wealth is an abundance of influence,
above even "that he lacks."
And it explains,
that these three matters
[the two matters in filling the lack and wealth]
exist also above
[and as is known48
that all matters below are drawn down from their counterpart above].
And the matter is,
that in the revelations above there are three levels in general.
Memaleh Kol Almin,
Sovev Kol Almin, and Atzmus Ein Sof that is above Memaleh and Sovev.
Memaleh Kol Almin is the light that is invested in the worlds and in the creations to give them life according to their worth.
And as our sages of blessed memory said49,
"Just as the soul fills the body, so the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the world,"
for just as the life of the soul that is invested in the body is according to the manner of the limbs of the body,
that in each limb the life is according to its worth,
so too is it regarding the life of Memaleh Kol Almin,
which gives life to each world and each creation according to its worth50.
And Sovev Kol Almin is the light that is above investment in the worlds,
therefore it surrounds and encompasses the worlds equally,
but it relates to the worlds
(therefore it is called by the name Sovev Kol Almin).
And it is analogous to the life of the soul itself,
that the soul is inherently alive,
for although it is incomparably above the life that spreads and is invested in the body,
nevertheless it is like a source from which the life that spreads and is invested in the body is drawn.
And this level is called by the name Chai Olamim
(Chai with a patach).
For the difference between Chai
(with a patach)
and Chei
(with a tzeirei)
is,
that in Chei Olamim with a tzeirei,
the word Chei is attached to Olamim,
meaning the life of the worlds — Memaleh,
and in Chai Olamim with a patach,
the word Chai is not attached to Olamim,
meaning the level of life in essence — Sovev.
And it can be said,
that this, that even the level of life in essence
(Sovev)
is called Chai Olamim, is because it is like a source from which the life of the worlds is drawn.
And the maamar adds51,
that the level of Sovev is also called by the name Chayei HaChayim.
For Chayim is the life that spreads and is invested in the worlds
(Memaleh),
and the level of Sovev from which the life of the worlds is drawn is called Chayei HaChayim.
And this is what our sages of blessed memory said52,
"May the Life-giver of life give you life,"
for "Life-giver of life"
(the level of Chayei HaChayim)
is the source from which lives are drawn.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that in the future, there will be a revelation of Atzmus Ein Sof, beyond even the level of Sovev, as indicated by the verse "on the third day He will raise us up."

translations.translation: And this is what our sages of blessed memory said53
on the verse54
"A psalm, a song for the Shabbos day,"
"A psalm, a song for the future to come, for a day that is entirely Shabbos and rest for the Life of the worlds,"
Chai HaOlamim with a patach55
is the level of Sovev,
and in the future to come there will be a cessation and rest even from the level of Chai HaOlamim,
for then there will be a revelation of Atzmus Ein Sof that is above relation to the worlds
(above even Sovev).
And as it is written56,
"He will give us life after two days; on the third day He will raise us up and we will live before Him,"
and it is brought in Likkutei Torah57
that the two days are the two revelations of Memaleh Kol Almin and Sovev Kol Almin, and the third day is the revelation of Atzmus Ein Sof that is above relation to the worlds.
For this is "on the third day He will raise us up and we will live before Him" — the inwardness and essence of Ein Sof.
[And it is noteworthy,
that the simple interpretation of "two days" and "third day" is that they are three time periods.
The two days are this world and the Garden of Eden, or this world and the days of Moshiach, and the third day is the Resurrection of the Dead58.
And the connection between the two interpretations is59,
that in the two time periods of the two days are the revelations of Memaleh and Sovev,
and at the Resurrection of the Dead there will be the revelation of the Essence].
